title: Back to New Orleans with Armstrong in 1931
summary: Armstrong hired him for the band after the Showboat broadcasts, with manager troubles and a gangster threat before the Suburban Gardens run.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: And I'll tell you one thing that really frightened me, and also the band. You see, in 31 we came down here and opened up at the Suburban Gardens. Well, we were broadcast from a place called the Showboat in Chicago, and they heard us, you know. So they engaged Louie to come down here and play. That's the time so many bands met us at the train, you know, at the big parade on Canal Street. Well, we were playing there, and a little bit of my story, Louie, about his time, began his popularity, began to climb, I'd say. I'd use that expression. And I was playing Savoy with H. and Tate, Chiquari in Chicago. And he came through, so in the mission he came over and talked to me, he said, well, he called me Nosy. He said, well, Nosy, I'm going to California, LA, and I'm going to the Sebastian's Cotton Club. And he used Les Heights band out there. He said, but I'll be back in about three months and I want you to play trombone for me. Well, I forgot all about it, so he did, truly his word. They're looking for me around, I live right around the corner from him, looking for me a couple of weeks, you know. And so finally, the guys around there knew he was looking for me. And so finally, they made contact and we start the rehearsals. So we go down the showboat and got a couple of weeks. And his former manager, Rockwell, he and Rockwell had some trouble. Anyhow, his manager later on was Dan Collins, who was a lawyer. So we were playing one night and it came a long distance call from New York. He went in the phone booth and there was a fellow who called a gangster called Foster. He went in there with him and put his gun on and said, come on, you're going back in New York. And Louis said, no, I'm not going back in New York. And he didn't. So thereafter, every night, he had to be a scooter by a squad call, you know. So we stayed there three months. And then we started doing this one night, through Michigan, Ohio, Kentucky. And so finally the word came, I said, where we going in New York? Well, I was glad to be in my hometown, you know. And that's when we came down and worked out there three months at Suburban Garden.
